claim: A frozen three-note lexical fixture passed 28 content checks across 41 completed CLI invocations and two owned server lifecycles. Both ai-memory 2.3.2 and Basic Memory 0.23.2 reflected writes, reads, updates and current-search deletion. ai-memory restart and native backup, and Basic Memory text-index rebuild, passed within their distinct scopes.
limitations: First ai-memory attempt failed the no-model-download constraint. A corrected run explicitly set its documented none embedding provider. No completed model files were found after stopping; transferred network bytes were not measured.

The already passing Basic Memory lane was reused, not rerun. Its source was pinned but dependencies resolved during installation rather than from an upstream lock; resolved package versions are retained.

ai-memory restore/reindex were not executed because their process guard checks sibling processes. Earlier separate restore receipts retain their own scope. Basic Memory reindex is not a lost-database restore.

Deletion checks do not establish erasure from version history, Git, logs or backups. No semantic-quality, cross-project isolation, hooks, live-client E2E, concurrency, timing advantage or universal winner is established.
This is the existing WSL host using isolated synthetic stores. No new physical-PC or fresh-WSL acceptance is implied; installed ai-memory binary/source equivalence was not rebuilt.
Public artifacts replace personal executable paths, normalize publication whitespace and withhold backup archive bytes. Original/public hashes and safe backup inventories retain provenance.
